newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty eases vs basket, one-day depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty eases vs basket, one-day depos flat.

text.p: The zloty weakened slightly against the basket of currencies on the back of a light currency buying trend prompted by expectations of the dollar's rise against the mark on the world markets, dealers said.
However, they said the zloty might rebound on client currency-sell orders and position closing at the end of the day and rise back to the three percent from trading band centre resistance level.
"There was some early speculative currency buying, but position closing may push the zloty back to the three percent from parity later today," said Pawel Lopuszynski from Pekao SA.

At 0910 GMT the zloty was quoted at 2.95/2.91 percent from the trading band centre, down from opening's 3.09/2.98 percent. It was at 3.0795/10 to the dollar against opening's 3.0790/20 and at 1.8004/11 to the mark, down from opening's 1.7955/75.
One-day deposits held flat after opening lower on a 579 million zloty net inflow into the system but an expected central bank drainage was seen underpinning them at above 21.50 percent.
Overnight deposit rates were flat at 21.50/21.90 percent, tomorrow/next rates were at 21.60/21.85 percent, down from Tuesday's close at 22.00/23.00 percent.
Players said expected large foreign demand at Wednesday's 800 million zloty fixed bond tender was likely to trigger zloty appreciation pressure before the settlement date on March 12.
Prices of the 12-percent five-year and 15-percent two-year bonds were expected to stay flat.

Poland's broad money rose by 679.1 million zlotys, or 0.5 percent, in February 1-20 to 136.72 billion after a 0.1 percent rise in the whole of January. Net foreign currency reserves fell by $29.5 million in February 1-10 to $21.44 billion.
